app_purpose: CSS transformation toolkit / parser (used by autoprefixer, cssnano, Tailwind, and most front-end build pipelines); the sink is source-map annotation parsing in lib/previous-map.js
root_cause: ReDoS / catastrophic regex backtracking in the source-map annotation regex (`/*# sourceMappingURL=... */`) in lib/previous-map.js loadAnnotation()/getAnnotationURL() (CWE-1333)

v0.ref: npm 8.2.9 (pre CVE-2021-23368). loadAnnotation regex `/\/\*\s*# sourceMappingURL=.*\s*\*\//gm` and getAnnotationURL `/\/\*\s*# sourceMappingURL=(.*)\s*\*\//` — the greedy `(.*)` immediately followed by `\s*` is ambiguous over a run of spaces (both match a space) and the required trailing `*/` never appears on the crafted input -> catastrophic backtracking.

v1.ref: npm 8.2.10 (CVE-2021-23368 fix = TARGET). Removed the `\s*` sub-pattern before `\*/` -> regex becomes `/\/\*\s*# sourceMappingURL=.*\*\//gm` (and `...=(.*)\*\//` in getAnnotationURL). This closes the whitespace-pad exponential, BUT the greedy `.*` remains: on a repeated `/*# sourceMappingURL=` prefix with no closing `*/`, `.*` scans to EOL and backtracks at every one of the many `/*` start positions -> O(n^2) residual ReDoS. INCOMPLETE FIX.
v1.base_url: http://127.0.0.1:28210 (Express service, POST /process; docker compose --profile v1 up -d)

v2.ref: npm 8.2.13 (CVE-2021-23382 fix). Replaced the greedy `.*` with a tempered-greedy token: loadAnnotation `/\/\*\s*# sourceMappingURL=(?:(?!sourceMappingURL=).)*\*\//gm` and getAnnotationURL `...=((?:(?!sourceMappingURL=).)*)\*\//`. The `(?:(?!sourceMappingURL=).)*` cannot cross a repeated `sourceMappingURL=` prefix, so the match cannot backtrack over the repeats -> residual closed (linear).

build.strategy: node:18-slim, `npm i express@4 postcss@<ver>` per profile via build-arg POSTCSS_VERSION (8.2.9/8.2.10/8.2.13). A REAL Express HTTP service (app/server.js) parses user-supplied CSS with the REAL published package on `POST /process`: `postcss.parse(req.body.css, {from:'/tmp/in.css', map:{prev:true}})` — parsing constructs a postcss Input -> a PreviousMap, whose constructor runs loadAnnotation(css) -> the source-map annotation regex (the documented sink), with no vendored/edited source. The regex runs SYNCHRONOUSLY on the Node event loop, so a catastrophic input HANGS the HTTP response (server-side ReDoS). The oracle triggers it via an EXTERNAL HTTP request and measures the round-trip latency.
build.host_safety: the ReDoS is observed as external HTTP latency with a 10s client read timeout (a hang is recorded as ~10000ms, never an unbounded host wait). Each container is cpus=1.0, mem_limit=512m, stop_grace_period=2s. Because a synchronous regex permanently wedges Node's single-threaded event loop (a running regex cannot be interrupted), the oracle measures every payload against a FRESH server (kill + `up -d` between probes) so a slow probe never poisons the next. Crafted CSS length is bounded (original 90025 chars, residual 504004 chars, benign 60 chars) — the blow-up is pure-CPU backtracking on a short input, flat memory.
build.harness_note: The Express service (app/server.js) does `const postcss=require('postcss')` (the package main entry, exported on all three versions) and exposes GET /health and POST /process {css} -> {ok, server_ms}. `postcss.parse(css,{from,map:{prev:true}})` is the public API path that reaches the same lib/previous-map.js loadAnnotation sink (Input -> PreviousMap -> loadAnnotation); the differential is the response latency of POST /process, triggered from OUTSIDE the container. (Note: the deprecated `"exports"` folder mapping in 8.2.9/8.2.10 only blocks extensionless SUBPATH requires like `postcss/lib/previous-map`; the bare `require('postcss')` main entry resolves fine, so no absolute-path hack is needed.)

mechanism.summary: postcss parses a `/*# sourceMappingURL=... */` annotation from CSS via a regex in lib/previous-map.js. (V0, 8.2.9) `loadAnnotation` uses `/\/\*\s*# sourceMappingURL=.*\s*\*\//gm` and `getAnnotationURL` uses `/\/\*\s*# sourceMappingURL=(.*)\s*\*\//`: the greedy `.*` is immediately followed by `\s*`, so over a run of spaces the two sub-patterns partition the same characters ambiguously, and because the required trailing `*/` is absent on the crafted input the engine backtracks catastrophically -> CVE-2021-23368. (V1, 8.2.10) The fix REMOVED the `\s*` between `.*` and `\*/` (`->` `...=.*\*\//`), which eliminates the space-run ambiguity and closes the whitespace-pad bomb. BUT the greedy `.*` was left intact: it still scans to end-of-line and must backtrack to find `*/`, and against a payload of many repeated `/*# sourceMappingURL=` prefixes with no closing `*/`, the global scan restarts a full `.*` backtrack at each `/*` start position -> O(n^2) blow-up -> CVE-2021-23382 (INCOMPLETE FIX). (V2, 8.2.13) The follow-up replaced `.*` with the tempered-greedy `(?:(?!sourceMappingURL=).)*`, which stops the match at the next `sourceMappingURL=` and therefore cannot backtrack across the repeats -> residual closed.
mechanism.original_sink: lib/previous-map.js loadAnnotation()/getAnnotationURL() regex — the `.*` + `\s*` ambiguity before the required `*/`
mechanism.residual_sink: lib/previous-map.js loadAnnotation()/getAnnotationURL() regex — the SAME greedy `.*` scanning-and-backtracking at each repeated `/*# sourceMappingURL=` start position
mechanism.guard_line_v1: let annotations = css.match(/\/\*\s*# sourceMappingURL=.*\*\//gm)   // CVE-2021-23368: `\s*` before `\*/` removed (greedy `.*` KEPT -> residual)
mechanism.original_redos_css: 'a{}/*# sourceMappingURL=' + ' '.repeat(90000) + '!'  (len 90025) — whitespace-pad, no `*/`; exercises the `.*`/`\s*` ambiguity
mechanism.residual_redos_css: 'a{}' + '/*# sourceMappingURL='.repeat(24000) + '!'  (len 504004) — repeated annotation prefix, no `*/`; greedy `.*` backtracks at every `/*` start
mechanism.benign_css: 'a{}/*# sourceMappingURL=data:application/json;base64,e30= */'  (len 60) — a well-formed inline sourceMappingURL data-URI annotation that matches cleanly (single prefix, real `*/` terminator)

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-15 to a REAL Express HTTP service (per HARD POLICY: no in-process library trigger). Built from the REAL published npm packages express@4 + postcss@8.2.9/8.2.10/8.2.13 on node:18-slim (no source edits). app/server.js exposes POST /process {css} -> `postcss.parse(css,{from:'/tmp/in.css',map:{prev:true}})` running SYNCHRONOUSLY on the event loop; parsing constructs an Input -> PreviousMap -> loadAnnotation, whose source-map annotation regex is the ReDoS sink. The ReDoS is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request and measured as server-side response latency. Regex evolution verified verbatim from each version's lib/previous-map.js (8.2.9 greedy `.*`+`\s*` before `*/`; 8.2.10 CVE-2021-23368 fix = removed `\s*`, greedy `.*` KEPT; 8.2.13 CVE-2021-23382 fix = tempered-greedy `(?:(?!sourceMappingURL=).)*`). Confirmed on real Docker (cpus=1.0, mem 512m, stop_grace 2s; FRESH server per probe so a wedged event loop never poisons the next): original whitespace-pad vector 'a{}/*# sourceMappingURL='+' 'x90000+'!' hangs on V0 (HTTP 10s timeout) and is ~6-7ms on V1 & V2; residual repeated-prefix vector 'a{}'+'/*# sourceMappingURL='x24000+'!' hangs on V0 AND on V1 (HTTP 10s timeout, INCOMPLETE FIX), ~7.9ms on V2; benign '...data:...base64,e30= */' <=6.7ms everywhere. residual V1/V2 latency separation ~1266x (well over 50x). Same source-map annotation regex, sequential ReDoS patches, distinct CVEs / distinct fixed versions (8.2.10 vs 8.2.13).
